annotations.text:
Quantities carry the screen

Total at 44px/700 tabular, each shop's number at 19px/700. Product name is 17px/600 — deliberately quieter than the number it labels.

Two signals, no colour beyond the five: Fill and edge say whether a line is done — white card = to pull, cream + Sage edge = settled. Contrast says whether it still wants you — Graphite means resolved, stop looking; full Ink means this needs attention.

So a short line wears the same cream and Sage as a completed one (it is done) and is the only settled card that has not gone quiet. Read the middle row of artboard 1: your eye lands on it with no colour involved.

Dusk budget: one

The only Dusk on the whole flow is the breathing dot on "Combined from 2 shop requests" — merging two shops into one walk is the one thing Tacet does here.

Every action is the picker's own, so the dispatch CTA is Ink, not Dusk. Filtered to one shop, nothing is combined and the Dusk line goes with it.

Why press-and-hold

Stock leaves the building here. A tap is one cold-thumb brush away from an accident, and a slide-to-confirm needs precision a gloved hand does not have.

A hold is deliberate, forgiving of a fat contact patch, and abortable by letting go.

Three ways a row can read

Same six lines, same data, three answers to "how many, for whom". B is built out on the Pick flow page; A and C are here to argue against it.

A buys list density and pays for it in the shop split. C makes both shop numbers huge by deleting the total, which is elegant until a third shop opens.
